To: lindqvist-family-blog
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: So I started a business!!!

Okay family, I have some news and I wanted you to hear it from me before Thanksgiving, partly because I love you and partly because I would like to eat Aunt Ruthie’s turkey without Dad giving me a presentation about health insurance.

I STARTED MY OWN PHOTOGRAPHY BUSINESS. It’s called Fernhollow Photo and it’s real and everything!!!

Rosebud Lane closed at the end of October. Marisol told me on October 6, and I spent a little while staring into space after that phone call. I’ve shot for her for four years, and it’s weird to think that chapter is over. I’m going to miss working with her so much.

Marisol basically taught me everything. She taught me how to keep my head when a wedding day gets chaotic, how to see the little moments happening while everyone’s looking somewhere else, and how to do this job without losing my mind completely. Mostly. She’s also been cheering me on through all of this, which means more than I can say. Love you, Marisol. Thank you for taking a chance on me.

So yes, this is a little scary! I’d be lying if I said I wasn’t nervous. But I’ve been planning this in my head for two years, and I do have a plan. I didn’t just wake up one morning and decide to throw a camera in the car and hope for the best. Although the car did play a part.

I filed the LLC on October 22, on my lunch break, sitting in the car outside Fred Meyer. Very glamorous beginning for Fernhollow Photo LLC. I cried a little afterward and then had to go back inside and be a normal person. The website went live November 1, which was another “stare at the screen and cry a little” moment. Apparently this is how I conduct business now.

And we already have 14 weddings booked for 2027!! Six couples came to me through Marisol, who has been incredibly generous with her referrals, and eight found me on their own. Four of those weddings are in June, so please check on my knees around July.

My first booking that was 100% mine was Dahlia and Ken at Timberline on June 12. They found me because of the Multnomah Falls couple pictures I shot for Marisol. They liked those pictures enough to trust me with their wedding day, and I still get a little teary thinking about it. I’m so excited to photograph them.

Jae will second shoot the big weddings with me and gets paid per wedding, so I won’t be trying to be in two places at once. I have tried that before and, unfortunately, it turns out I cannot.

And DAD: health insurance is sorted. I picked a marketplace plan and it starts January 1. You can still ask me about it, obviously, but please enjoy your turkey first.

The name is my favorite part. Fernhollow comes from the fern hollow trail behind Grandma’s old place in Gresham, where I took my first real pictures with her Pentax. Grandma, I named it for you. You let me borrow your camera and wander around looking at everything, and I don’t think either of us knew where that would lead. I wish I could show those first pictures to everyone, although I’m pretty sure at least half of them were just ferns. Very on brand, it turns out.

Sam made me a cake to celebrate and had them write FERNHOLLOW on it, except the cake said FERNHOLOW. We ate it anyway. It was excellent and I’m choosing to believe the missing L is lucky. Sam has been so good at talking me down when I start thinking about everything all at once, and I’m really glad he’s in my corner.

I know this is a big change, but I’m really excited. I get to make something of my own doing work I love, and I have a head start, a plan, and some very good people helping me. I wanted to share it with all of you because you’ve been cheering me on for a long time too.

Also! Does anyone want free family pictures at Thanksgiving? I’ll bring my camera to Ruthie’s if people are up for it. We can do a big group one and a few smaller ones, and I promise to be quicker than I was at Christmas. Uncle Greg, you can tell me if you’re freezing.

Love you guys. See you in Salem!!
